newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB raises Australia wheat estimate to 21 m/t.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB raises Australia wheat estimate to 21 m/t.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said it had increased its estimate of the 1996/97 Australian wheat crop to 21 million tonnes from 20 million tonnes.
This reflected increased estimates from all states except Western Australia, the AWB said in its weekly grain market report.

Queensland was now expected to produce 1.9 million tonnes up from 1.7 million tonnes in the previous forecast, New South Wales 7.0 million tonnes (up from 6.5 million tonnes), Victoria 2.5 million tonnes (up from 2.4 million tonnes) and South Australia 2.7 million tonnes (2.5 million tonnes).
Forecast production from Western Australia remained steady at 6.9 million tonnes, AWB said.
The increased forecast comes about a month after the AWB increased its forecast to 20 million from 19 million tonnes.
Soon after that forecast AWB deputy chairman Rob Barry said the forecast may still be "a bit light on".

Australian traders and brokers have been unofficially forecasting an Australian wheat crop of up to 22 million tonnes for some months. The AWB's latest official forecast now puts it near the top end of the range of forecasts for the Australian crop.
The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) on October 22 increased its 1996/97 forecast to 20.9 million tonnes from its previous forecast of 18.8 million tonnes.
In 1995/96 Australia produced almost 17.0 million tonnes of wheat.
